entities.summary: The Sagrestia Vecchia di San Lorenzo, or Old Sacristy of San Lorenzo, is the older of two sacristies of the Basilica of San Lorenzo in Florence, Italy. It is one of the most important monuments of early Italian Renaissance architecture. Designed by Filippo Brunelleschi and paid for by the Medici family, who also used it for their tombs, it set the tone for the development of a new style of architecture that was built around proportion, the unity of elements, and the use of the classical orders. historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Sagrestia Vecchia di San Lorenzo's design by Filippo Brunelleschi influenced the development of Italian Renaissance architecture, setting a new standard for proportion and classical orders. Its construction by the Medici family also showcased their patronage of the arts.
